messages.subject: Re: Prepping the dataset
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sofia,
No, you do not need all the columns listed in the bookdown.
You can directly create yourself a dataset with the same structure as the aggregated dataset, thereby bypassing the need to use the function `prepsources()`.
So one line per location and source_ID (a name for the location, can also be the lat and long pasted together or anything else), mean_source_value (the mean dC13 at the location), var_source_value (the variance across dC13 measurements at the location), n_source_value (the sample size at the location), lat (the latitude), long (the longitude).
That assumes that you have some replicates per sampling location.
If that is not the case, please let me know.
Best,
Alex

On Friday 28 June 2024 at 14:22:10 UTC+2 sofia.f...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi colleagues,
>
> I am new to IsoriX and I am hoping to be able to use it for my masters project, though I am not sure if my data is suitable. A background to my project is that I am trying to assign the migratory origin of breeding turtles using tissue isotopes, first by building an isoscape based on the turtle skin carbon isotope signatures of turtles from known locations. It is a simple dataset with 4 columns (turtle_ID, lat, long, dC13). As it does not contain all the columns listed in the bookdown, does this mean I am unable to use this package or can things be modified?
>
> Many thanks in advance,
> Sofia
